digest.component_or_area: MCP and review-bot service startup/initialization and per-operation composition
propositions: MCP and review-bot must capture non-secret startup config and policy exactly once per service startup, preventing inconsistent rereads of static material across long-running operations.

Each operation or request must receive a fresh, non-secret OperationSnapshot composed at call time, while inbound bearer tokens remain request-scoped and never enter startup snapshots, operation snapshots, logs, caches, or child environments.

Review-bot must validate decision-bearing auth (gerrit_bot_token, GitHub credentials) before accepting a job or webhook, raising DecisionAuthError on missing/blank/conflicting/revoked credentials with no fallback principal, and forward the composed LLMRuntime through the code review decision path.

Startup bindings (frozen .llm_runtime, non-secret .policy) must remain stable across ambient file/environment mutations; a restarted process observes the new material, and native SDK-owned refreshable capabilities maintain their SDK-driven refresh semantics.

Partial or rejected Langfuse/OTLP telemetry credentials must disable telemetry fail-open with redacted diagnostics, leaving the underlying operation result unchanged, while security-bearing auth remains fail-closed.
MCP inbound bearer/OAuth tokens and OperationSnapshot.build must reject secret-typed leaves, ensuring credentials never leak into canonical snapshot bytes or startup composition.
